newsitem.title: UK: UK agents back Lufthansa Cargo shipper plan.
newsitem.headline: UK agents back Lufthansa Cargo shipper plan.

text.p: UK freight forwarders have reacted positively to a Lufthansa proposal that forwarders and carriers deal jointly with shippers, Lufthansa Cargo AG UK and Ireland marketing manager Ruediger Helm said.
The plan was first put forward by Lufthansa Cargo's UK/Ireland director Bob Bingley in November 1995 seeking a "tripartite relationship" between LCAG, forwarders and shippers

"This is a continuing, evolving process but the reaction so far from forwarders to our initiative has been very good. We have so far contacted 30 major UK forwarders with this proposal and only two responses have been negative," Helm told Reuters.

MSAS Cargo International, Burlington Air Express, AEI, Circle International, Trans Global, Wilson & Co (UK) and Emery Worldwide were among the forwarders which had welcomed Lufthansa Cargo's proposal of a tripartite airline-agent-shipper relationship.
"The reasoning behind this new relationship is to help us provide the type of quality service that is required by the shipper," he said.
Helm stressed that LCAG was opposed to the approach being adopted by carriers such as KLM, which focused on direct dealing with shippers in certain circumstances.

"Air cargo, particularly in the UK, is very much a freight forwarder-driven industry. Forwarders are responsible for providing more than 90 percent of our business and we do not see this changing. The KLM approach is not our approach," he said.
Helm added that UK forwarders which had responded positively to Lufthansa Cargo's initiative had passed on the names of their top shipper clients to the airline.

LCAG had written to these shippers requesting information on the nature of their products, their main cargo destinations, the freight volumes they book, the amount of business they conduct with Lufthansa, the structure of their shipments - for example if they preferred consolidated or express shipments - and their preferred delivery times.

"We have since had meetings between the airline, a forwarder and a shipper. These have virtually all focused on the demands...the service standards required by shippers. Pricing has not come into it," he said. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 547 7706 Fax 5017
